question.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 18 \\ 39\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -6 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 18 \\ 39\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -6 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+18{x}_{2}=-6 \\ 5{x}_{1}+39{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -3 \\ 3 & 18 & -6 \\ 5 & 39 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 5 & 39 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & k+15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & k+15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & k+19\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+19.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+19\,⇒\,k=-19.
$$
